reason: E1 directly demonstrates that a Zr-Cr micro-diffusion layer enhances bonding and provides protection in both aqueous and high-temperature oxidation tests, supporting the first two premises. However, no cited evidence shows that this layer reduces interdiffusion-driven failure or improves durability under steam conditions; E4 and E5 discuss Cr coating performance and interdiffusion but do not test the proposed intermediate layer, leaving the third and fourth premises unsupported.
premises: A Zr-Cr micro-diffusion layer enhances interface bonding strength between Cr coating and Zr-4 alloy.
Cr coatings with a Zr-Cr micro-diffusion layer protect Zr-4 alloy in both long-term aqueous (420 °C) and high-temperature isothermal oxidation (900–1300 °C) tests.
The proposed intermediate layer reduces the risk of premature coating failure due to elevated-temperature Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
The intervention improves durability under both normal subcritical-water and accident-relevant high-temperature steam conditions.
